newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Turnover on the slide on Bucharest stock exchange.
newsitem.headline: Turnover on the slide on Bucharest stock exchange.

text.p: Turnover on the Bucharest stock exchange sagged to 31.2 million lei on Thursday, a little more than half the previous level, as demand stayed low and supply was even lower.
"Interest was thin. Buyers focused on a few stocks as demand for others could not be met by supply," said a trader.
Seven stocks drifted higher, three touched new lows, one closed flat and three had no transaction.
Fertiliser maker Azomures SA, seen as the bourse's most attractive stock, stayed in the limelight, getting 74 percent of turnover. It closed 100 lei higher at 11,000.
Artrom SA also caught investors' interest. One third of the total 4,826 shares traded on Thursday were Artrom shares. The engineering company closed 100 lei weaker at 2,000.
"A recent announcement that Artrom mass privatisation shares can now be traded on the bourse did not make any difference in supply, which was rather short," a broker said.

Under a mass selloff launched a year ago Romanians could swap privatisation paper for stakes of up to 60 percent in 4,000 state companies. Some 1,600 Romanians opted for Artrom shares getting 60,000 shares for their coupons.
Brokers said trading on Thursday remained unimpressed by a presidential run-off due on Sunday.
"There is little, if any, news that can actually move this market," said a trader.
Two unofficial value-weighted indices -- the VAB, computed by Vanguard SA securities, and Bucharest Investment Group 's BIG -- rose from the previous session by 0.7 percent each.
Prices are on MRRO and MRRP.
